question: Is a hospital trade association HOSPITAL_AFFILIATED_ENTITY or NONPROFIT_CBO under spec 8?
why_it_is_open: Spec 10.2 hospital-association row prescribes NONPROFIT_CBO, and that is what Alaska (Alaska Hospital & Healthcare Association, 4 awards) and Illinois (ICAHN) already use. Georgia hand-coded this row HOSPITAL_AFFILIATED_ENTITY in session 9, before that row existed, making it the outlier of three. Session 18 found the divergence and deliberately did not resolve it (re-coding a committed hand-coded row to satisfy a rule added the same day is how spec 2.1 regressions happen). Session 19 fixed the half that was a code defect -- HOSPITAL_AFFILIATED_ENTITY no longer short-circuits to DIRECT/Yes, so the shared classifier and Georgia now AGREE on the flow (IN_KIND_BENEFIT, distributed_to_hospital = No). What is left is purely the spec 8 typing question, which is a human call: it decides how the NEXT state codes an association, and Georgia is the only committed row it would touch.
dollar_effect: $0. The row carries no amount (Georgia publishes per initiative, not per recipient) and is distributed_to_hospital = No under either type, so neither bucket of rhtp_hospital_dollar_partition() moves whichever way it is settled. Decide it on the spec, not on the total.

question: Which of the 22 Kansas recipients whose organisational form KDHE never states are hospitals under spec 8?
options: HOSPITAL_OR_SYSTEM | HOSPITAL_AFFILIATED_ENTITY | NONPROFIT_CBO (the current coding) | FQHC_OR_RHC
why_it_is_open: KDHE publishes a recipient and an amount and nothing about the recipient's form -- it has no organisation-type column of the kind Oregon and Alaska both publish. So rhtp_classify_recipient_type() falls back to spec 8's standing answer on 22 of 46 rows. Several read as hospitals to anyone who knows Kansas (Stormont Vail Health, AdventHealth Ottawa, Labette Health, South Central Kansas Health -- which KDHE's own project text calls "Kansas' first REH") and several plainly are not (Special Olympics Kansas, InterHab, the Kansas Council on Developmental Disabilities). Promoting the first group on this pipeline's own knowledge is the spec 0.4 failure the project exists to avoid, so nothing was promoted. This is what the CCN match is for (open blocker 5).
dollar_effect: $39,249,763 across 22 rows, against a confirmed named-hospital floor of $35,721,277 -- the uncertainty is LARGER than the figure it sits beside.

question: Which of the 24 Maryland recipients whose organisational form MDH never states are hospitals under spec 8 -- and are the two typed HOSPITAL_OR_SYSTEM from their names actually FQHCs?
options: HOSPITAL_OR_SYSTEM | HOSPITAL_AFFILIATED_ENTITY | NONPROFIT_CBO (the current coding) | FQHC_OR_RHC
why_it_is_open: MDH publishes a recipient, an amount, a project summary and the counties served, and NOTHING about the recipient's organisational form -- it has no organisation-type column of the kind Oregon and Alaska both publish. So every recipient_type is derived from the recipient's own NAME, and rhtp_classify_recipient_type() falls back to spec 8's standing answer on 24 of 41 rows. THIS ONE RUNS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, WHICH KANSAS'S DOES NOT. Understated: TidalHealth ($4,911,052) and Meritus Health Center ($3,583,406) are among the 24, and spec 0.3a names TidalHealth as a hospital -- neither is counted in Maryland's hospital figure today. Overstated: Choptank Community Health System Inc ($1,976,042) and Mountain Laurel Medical Center ($1,058,750) are typed HOSPITAL_OR_SYSTEM from their names and are, on the ordinary reading, FQHCs -- both ARE counted today. Promoting or demoting either group on this pipeline's own knowledge is the spec 0.4 failure the project exists to avoid, so NOTHING WAS PROMOTED and nothing was demoted. This is what the CCN match is for (open blocker 5). Note also that all 41 Maryland rows are award OFFERS, not executed agreements (MDH's own word), so every figure here is NOTICE_OF_INTENT_TO_AWARD + amount_confirmed = No.
dollar_effect: $36,558,089 across 24 rows, against a named-hospital floor of $14,678,864 -- the uncertainty is two and a half times the figure it sits beside, and unlike Kansas it can move the figure DOWN as well as up: $3,034,792 of today's $14,678,864 sits on the two names that read as FQHCs.

question: Which of the 30 Nebraska recipients whose organisational form DHHS never states are hospitals under spec 8?
options: HOSPITAL_OR_SYSTEM | HOSPITAL_AFFILIATED_ENTITY | NONPROFIT_CBO (the current coding) | FQHC_OR_RHC
why_it_is_open: Nebraska DHHS publishes a recipient and an amount on each of its three notices of award and NOTHING about the recipient's organisational form -- it has no organisation-type column of the kind Oregon and Alaska both publish. So outside the 21 Nebraska High Value Network member rows, every recipient_type is derived from the recipient's own NAME, and rhtp_classify_recipient_type() falls back to spec 8's standing answer on 30 of the 57 award rows. Several read as hospitals to anyone who knows Nebraska: CHI St. Mary's ($908,475.54), CHI Health Schuyler ($711,629.63), Faith Health ($578,673.70), CHI Good Samaritan/CHI St. Francis ($430,601.57), Mary Lanning Healthcare ($460,239.40), CHI Health Plainview ($355,311.03), Methodist Fremont Health ($334,176.13), Jefferson Community Health & Life ($446,741.33), Gothenburg Health ($309,749.28), Memorial Health Care System ($339,999.92), Boone County Health Center ($340,000.00) and Syracuse Area Health ($200,000.00); several plainly are not (the four community colleges are typed UNIVERSITY_OR_AHC already, but United Way of Western Nebraska, Lutheran Family Services and Blue Valley Community Action sit in the 30). THE EVIDENCE A REVIEWER SHOULD START FROM IS ALREADY IN THE REPOSITORY, AND IT IS WHY THIS ROW IS NOT SIMPLY A REPEAT OF KANSAS'S. DHHS's Initiative 4.4b notice names 21 organisations under its own sentence "The list of individual hospitals receiving funding as of the time of this notice follows" -- so for those names the STATE has stated the form. Four of the 30 appear on that roster under a near-identical name: Boone County Health Center and Gothenburg Health exactly, 'Jefferson Community Health and Life' against the award table's 'Jefferson Community Health & Life', and 'Memorial Health Care Systems' against 4.4a's 'Memorial Health Care System'. Those last two differ by one character across two documents, which is precisely the fuzzy hospital match spec 2 forbids a machine from auto-resolving -- so nothing was promoted and the match is left for a human. Promoting any of the 30 on this pipeline's own knowledge is the spec 0.4 failure the project exists to avoid. This is also what the CCN match is for (open blocker 5). Note that the Nebraska Hospital Association, named as a subrecipient in Nebraska's CMS project abstract, is on NONE of the three notices of award and so is not among these 30 or anywhere in the file.
dollar_effect: $9,411,695.59 across 30 rows, against a named-hospital floor of $6,990,996.01 -- the uncertainty is LARGER than the figure it sits beside, as in Kansas and Maryland. It runs mainly upward: the CHI Health entities, Mary Lanning, Methodist Fremont and Faith Health alone are $3,069,507.40 of it. Deliberately EXCLUDED from this figure is the Nebraska High Value Network's own row ($18,156,856.12), which also carries spec 8's fallback for its corporate form but whose dollars are already attributed to hospitals under POOL_NAMED_HOSPITALS by spec 10.2, on DHHS's own sentence, whichever way its form is settled.
